subject: Model Consultation on change point model in RStan

messages.author: 4e354edaa049aeeb
messages.subject: Model Consultation on change point model in RStan
parts:
Has anybody fitted a change point model in Stan, please?

We are interested to fit a change point (broken stick) model in RStan to model longitudinal continuous outcomes measured about three to ten times (at baseline and follow-ups) for each of about hundreds of subjects (i.e. patients in a clinical trial); (So this is different from a time series on a single outcome for a single unit of observation, say a NYSE stock.). The timing of the outcome observations is different for each individual (the patients come in for appointments at different, irregularly), as are the slopes before and after the change point, the intercept and the actual change point itself.

The model:

y[i,k] = beta[pre, i] * (t[i, k] – tau[i]) * I(t[i, k] < tau[i]) + beta[intercept, i]+ beta[post, i] * (t[i,k] – tau[i]) * I(t[i,k] > tau[i]) + epsilon[i,j]

where the error term epsilon [i,k] ~MVN (0, Sigma), iid;

y[i,j,t] is the continuous outcome of the ith subject at the kth observation at time t[i,k]; beta[pre,i] is the random slope for each subject before,  beta[post,i] is the random slope for each subject after the subject specific change point tau. We think a reasonable prior for beta may be ~MVN, iid, but the slopes and intercept are certainly not iid.

 I( t[i,k] > tau[i]) is the indicator function used to define a linear spline: (t[i, k] – tau[i]) * I(t[i, k] < tau[i]) = t[i,k] - tau[k]  iff t[i,k] < tau[i] ; 0 otherwise;

tau [i] is the random change point (to be estimated for each subject i); tau [i] is the time of the ‘kink’ in the spline measured before say a diagnosis of dementia.;

See for example attached: Hall CB, Ying J, Kuo L, Sliwinski M, Buschke H, Katz M, Lipton RB. Estimation of bivariate measurements having different change points, with application to cognitive ageing. Stat Med. 2001 Dec 30;20(24):3695-714. PubMed PMID: 11782027.

We are interested to learn from similar models other users may have fitted or know about or to share related functions, now possible in Rstan.

Thank you.

Michael Andreae

messages.author: 3f22b207863d2049
messages.subject: Re: Model Consultation on change point model in RStan
parts:
There is a recent discussion about a change point model, although that one seemed simpler than the one you propose: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/stan-users/QlgX00f6JG8. Nevertheless, it might provide some inspiration.

In short, you will probably have to specify a mixture model, marginalizing over the different possible values of the changing point in time for each individual.

Luc
